identity.name: South Kasai
alt_names: Autonomous Mining State of South Kasai

land.text: south-eastern Kasai: Kalonji 'declared the region of south-eastern Kasai to be the new Mining State'; the declared borders 'included all of Kasai Province except Sankuru District and Lulua District' but the Kalonjists controlled 'a much smaller portion of territory'
Bakwanga (Mbuji-Mayi) and its surroundings, entered by central government troops on 5 October 1962

capitals.name: Bakwanga (Mbuji-Mayi)
capitals.note: 'The state's capital was Bakwanga'; the coordinates are the gazetteer's for Mbuji-Mayi, 'later renamed'.

rulers.name: Albert Kalonji
rulers.title: President, later Mulopwe (king)
rulers.note: 'Kalonji was declared president and Joseph Ngalula prime minister'; Kalonji took the title Mulopwe on 16 July 1961 and the state became the Federated Kingdom of South Kasai; arrested in December 1961, escaped on 7 September 1962, fled after the coup of 29-30 September 1962.

correction.text: The Kalonjist core round Bakwanga; the declared borders 'included all of Kasai Province except Sankuru District and Lulua District' but the state 'actually controlled a much smaller portion of territory'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The page gives no area and no map of what was held; the 100 km radius round Bakwanga (about 31,000 km2) is the researcher's reading of 'a much smaller portion'. The declared extent is Kasai Province less two districts, which the gazetteer has no names for.

region.text: south-eastern Kasai, the Mining State of South Kasai

ledger.note: 1960: Albert Kalonji declares the Mining State of South Kasai. 'On 9 August 1960, Kalonji, still in Katanga, declared the region of south-eastern Kasai to be the new Mining State'; the Congo Crisis page dates it 8 August. Capital Bakwanga; 'Kalonji was declared president and Joseph Ngalula prime minister'. The extent is the researcher's reading.

1961: Kalonji takes the royal title Mulopwe (16 July 1961, after his father's 12 April bestowal) and 'the state's title then changed to the Federated Kingdom of South Kasai'. Same state and land (rule 2); the page gives no month for the change of title.

1962: the central army returns to Bakwanga and the secession ends. 'On 5 October 1962, central government troops again arrived in Bakwanga' after a coup against the Kalonjist regime on the night of 29-30 September 1962; infobox 'Dissolution: 5 October 1962'. Kalonji 'fled to Paris'.

region.text: South Kasai returned to the central government

ledger.note: 5 October 1962: South Kasai ends; its land passes to the Congo (identity.successors). Parliament had 'given South Kasai official provincial status' on 9 March 1962.

wars.name: South Kasai secession in the Congo Crisis
wars.outcome: ANC soldiers arrived in Bakwanga on 27 August 1960 and in the massacres 'around 3,000 Baluba were killed' ('a case of incipient genocide', Hammarskjöld); the state survived until the coup of 29-30 September and the army's return on 5 October 1962.
wars.note: The page dates South Kasai's start 9 August 1960; the Congo Crisis page has 8 August.

certainty.note: The declared border (Kasai Province less Sankuru and Lulua districts) was larger than the land the Kalonjists held; the pages give no map of the held land.

sources.title: South Kasai
sources.note: Proclamation 9 August 1960, Bakwanga, declared and actual territory, ANC arrival 27 August 1960, Mulopwe 1961, Kalonji arrested December 1961, coup 29-30 September 1962, dissolution 5 October 1962.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks, written as the rebel counterpart of the DRC dossier (loss August 1960, gain October 1962). One page opened (the Congo Crisis page, opened for the DRC dossier, is cited in the DRC ledger for the same dates and gives 8 August for the start, 5 October for the end). Discrepancies: start 9 August (South Kasai page) against 8 August (Congo Crisis page); Kalonji's arrest 30 December 1961 (infobox) against removal of immunity on 2 December 1961 (body). The extent held is the researcher's reading: no page gives area or towns beyond Bakwanga. Gap-filler: a page on the Baluba conflict or Kasai Province's districts would replace the radius. Family 'africa' is a placeholder for the colour agent.
